veranderings.blok: Werk wat al honderde jare aanhou
veranderings.rede: Two adjectives of equal value before a noun are separated by a comma (AWS).

veranderings.blok: Werk wat al honderde jare aanhou
veranderings.voor: Mense maak vandag nog kleipotte, en vandag nog mandjies uit gras.
veranderings.na: Mense maak vandag nog kleipotte en mandjies uit gras.
veranderings.rede: The second part has no subject or verb of its own, so the comma before 'en' is wrong under AWS, and the repeated 'vandag nog' reads wooden.

veranderings.voor: Nat klei is sag en jy vorm dit
veranderings.na: Nat klei is sag, en jy vorm dit
veranderings.rede: 'en' joins two sentences each with its own subject and verb, so AWS requires a comma.

veranderings.voor: Die klei het ander eienskappe gekry en die pot is nou
veranderings.na: Die klei het ander eienskappe gekry, en die pot is nou
veranderings.rede: 'en' joins two sentences each with its own subject and verb, so AWS requires a comma.

veranderings.voor: Bakstene begin ook by nat klei.
veranderings.na: Bakstene begin ook as nat klei.
veranderings.rede: 'begin by' means start at a place; 'begin as' is the natural way to say bricks start out as wet clay.
'By ... bygemeng' repeats 'by' awkwardly; 'Vir hierdie stene' states clearly which bricks the mix is for.

veranderings.voor: Die steen kraak dan baie minder maklik wanneer hy droog word.
veranderings.na: Die stene kraak dan baie minder maklik wanneer hulle droog word.
veranderings.rede: The previous sentence speaks of 'hierdie stene' in the plural, so the singular 'Die steen ... hy' breaks the reference.

veranderings.voor: Groen halms krimp later in die mandjie.
veranderings.na: Groen halms sou later in die mandjie krimp.
veranderings.rede: The sentence gives the reason for drying first; 'sou' makes clear it is what would happen to green stalks, not what happens to the dried ones in the basket.
Singular 'palmblaar' used as a mass noun reads unnatural; the plural is the usual form.

veranderings.voor: Vir baie matte bind gare die halms langs mekaar vas.
veranderings.na: Vir baie matte word die halms met gare langs mekaar vasgebind.
veranderings.rede: Making the thread the subject that ties is wooden; the passive with 'met gare' is the natural construction and keeps the meaning.

veranderings.na: is sterker as een halm alleen.
veranderings.rede: 'enige halm' can be read as any stalk at all, including those in the mat; 'een halm alleen' says clearly a single loose stalk.

veranderings.voor: Die hele dak lê skuins en die droë halms
veranderings.na: Die hele dak lê skuins, en die droë halms
veranderings.rede: 'en' joins two sentences each with its own subject and verb, so AWS requires a comma.

veranderings.voor: hou daardie nat buitekant ver van die binnekant af.
veranderings.na: hou daardie nat buitekant weg van die binnekant.
veranderings.rede: 'iets weg hou van' is the natural idiom for keeping something away; 'ver van ... af hou' reads stiff.

veranderings.voor: Mense kies meestal die materiaal vir wat sy eienskappe kan doen.
veranderings.na: Mense kies 'n materiaal meestal oor wat sy eienskappe kan doen.
veranderings.rede: 'kies vir wat' copies English 'for what'; Afrikaans chooses 'oor' something, and 'n materiaal' is the general case meant here.

veranderings.voor: en word hard in die vuur.
veranderings.na: en word in die vuur hard.
veranderings.rede: In Afrikaans the complement 'hard' naturally stands at the end, after the place phrase.

veranderings.voor: Die eienskap kom eerste en die gebruik volg daaruit.
veranderings.na: Die eienskap kom eerste, en die gebruik volg daaruit.
veranderings.rede: 'en' joins two sentences each with its own subject and verb, so AWS requires a comma.

vlae.teks: Die lang dun stingel ... / 'n Hoë grasagtige plant met lang dun stingels ...
vlae.rede: By the same AWS rule as 'gladde, ronde klippie', these glossary definitions would take a comma between equal adjectives ('lang, dun'); not proposed as changes because these terms may be shared with other lessons, so a person should decide it subject-wide.

vlae.teks: 'n Hoë grasagtige plant met lang dun stingels wat mense verwerk.
vlae.rede: 'wat mense verwerk' can attach to the stems or to the plant; fixing it would mean guessing which is meant, and the definition may be shared.

vlae.teks: Die halms lê in dik lae op mekaar. ... Die dik laag hou daardie nat buitekant ...
vlae.rede: The text moves from plural 'lae' to singular 'Die dik laag' and 'die hele laag'; it reads as the thatch as a whole, but a writer should confirm the number is intended.
